I'm **Domenico Guadalupi**, the engineer and data scientist behind
web<span class="webgeods-wordmark-geo">Geo</span>DS. I take on remote
projects in three areas: automating GIS workflows (in ArcGIS or with
open-source tools), checking the quality of spatial data, and spatial
analysis that reports its own uncertainty. Every project has a fixed
price agreed before I start, and you keep the code.

::: {.wwm-packages .column-page}

::: {.wwm-package}
[Data quality]{.wwm-eyebrow}

### Automated GIS data quality check

**For** teams that maintain network, asset or parcel layers and check
them by hand, or not at all.

**What I do**: a script that checks your layers against your own
rules: geometry validity, topology (overlaps, gaps, dangling or
unconnected lines), missing or inconsistent attributes, coordinate
system. Every problem is reported with its location.

**You get** a report (spreadsheet plus a layer of the flagged
features), the script, and instructions to run it again on the next
delivery. It runs in ArcGIS Pro (arcpy) or in plain Python or R.

**Proof**: at a fibre network design company I designed and largely
wrote the QA automation for network designs; a check that took a day
now takes half an hour. On this site:
[Validate](/tools/geojson-shapefile-validator.html) ·
[Check Topology](/tools/topology-checker.html) ·
[Network from Lines](/tools/network-from-lines.html).

[From €300 · one dataset, up to about 10 rules · about a week]{.wwm-price}
:::

::: {.wwm-package}
[Automation]{.wwm-eyebrow}

### ArcGIS workflow automation

**For** a task in ArcGIS Pro or ArcGIS Online that someone repeats by
hand every week: exports, updates to hosted layers, styling, maps or
reports generated from the data.

**What I do**: turn it into a script tool, a Python toolbox or a
scheduled notebook (ArcGIS API for Python), in your environment and
with your licence. Open-source tools if you don't use Esri.

**You get** the working tool, short documentation, and a handover
call to walk your team through it.

**Proof**: at the same company, generating layer styles (SLD) from
the network layers went from three days of manual work to a few
hours. More on my [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/guadalupi).

[From €300 · one operation as a script tool · about a week]{.wwm-price}
:::

::: {.wwm-package}
[Spatial analysis]{.wwm-eyebrow}

### Interpolation with an uncertainty map

**For** point samples (soil, groundwater, air quality, sensor
readings) that need to become a continuous surface you can defend.

**What I do**: exploratory analysis, a variogram fitted to your data,
kriging (or cokriging with a correlated covariate), and
cross-validation to measure how well it predicts.

**You get** two maps, the prediction and its uncertainty, as
GeoTIFFs; a short report on the method and its validation; and the
R or Python code to reproduce it.

**Proof**: [Kriging Interpolator](/tools/kriging-interpolator.html) ·
[Raster Gap Filler](/tools/raster-gap-filler.html), and the article
[Interpolating Soil Moisture with Kriging](/posts/kriging-soil-sampling.html).

[From €350 · one variable, one study area · about a week]{.wwm-price}
:::

:::

The prices above are for the smallest version of each job. More rules,
more datasets or a complete workflow: you get a fixed quote, with a
delivery date, once I've seen a sample of the data.

## How it works

::: {.wwm-steps}
1. **You describe the task**: what you do today, a sample of the data
   or a description of it if it's confidential.
2. **We agree the scope**: by email or in a short call, I confirm what
   is included and what isn't.
3. **You get a fixed quote** within two working days. No hourly
   billing, no surprises.
4. **I deliver**: results, code and instructions, with one round of
   revisions included.
:::

Your data stays confidential: I can sign an NDA, and nothing from a
project is published without your written permission.

## Something else?

Spatial machine learning with honest validation (see the
[Spatial Classifier](/tools/spatial-classifier.html)), turning line
layers into networks, custom checks for your data model: if it's
spatial data and it repeats, write anyway. If it isn't a good fit,
I'll tell you.
